title: Icon task tests create Feast rows before suppressing the eager post-save task
reasoning: These tests run with CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER enabled, but they create Feast objects before patching the icon matcher or otherwise disconnecting the post-save handler. If Feast creation triggers match_icon_to_feast_task through the signal, the real eager task can run during setup before the test's mock is installed, causing duplicate matching, unexpected DB state, external-service work, or flaky assertions. The designation tests explicitly disconnect the same feast save signal during setup, which indicates this signal side effect is expected to matter in eager tests.
recommendation: Disconnect handle_feast_save around Feast creation in these task tests, or patch the signal-dispatched task before creating the Feast. Prefer a helper/context manager so every Feast fixture used by direct task tests is created without eager signal side effects.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current tests assert the explicit direct call to match_icon_to_feast_task, but they do not assert that setup was side-effect free or that the signal did not already run before the mocked matcher was installed.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that patches hub.signals.match_icon_to_feast_task.delay before creating a Feast in this test class and asserts it is not called during fixture setup, or refactor setup to disconnect the signal and assert the direct task invocation is the only matcher call.
